original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In F2 of the semidihedral group of order 16, with paid labels {r, r^{-1}, s} and all six rank-one idempotents on exactly two registers, the shortest call word for diag([r^4], [e]) is 4 and the shortest call word for diag([r^4], [r^4]) is 8.
scope_change_reason: The card allows one specified nonabelian operation family. This package fixes the semidihedral presentation s r s = r^3, the three-label alphabet, width two, and the two central targets. It is not the abelian three-register model, and it is not the order-16 dihedral involution alphabet of discussion 1818.
bottleneck_link: The complex primitive binds and the bit primitive does not. A shorter central word would still need a full supplier bill before it could move kappa. This alphabet's exact two-register bill equals the coordinate construction, so there is no local saving to price. The result is a scoped obstruction for this address family, not a headline exponent change.
stop_rule: Stop after the two-register radius-4 certificate. Do not continue to three registers once the radius-4 enumeration exceeds memory.
evidence: PASS_SEMIDIHEDRAL_CENTRAL_TWO_ROLE one=4 two=8 ball4=25149 gates=18 layers=1,18,213,2276,22641 controls=6 no_new_kappa. Both Python -B and Python -O runs agree. The regular representation is faithful, and a separate group-algebra matrix checker agrees on every gate and on both witnesses. One upstream discussion write was forbidden (Resource not accessible by integration) and was not retried.
author: AI-assisted research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used for the overlap search, the exhaustive checker, and this write-up.

open_questions.question: Can one restored third register reduce diag([r^4], [r^4], [e]) below eight calls in this same semidihedral alphabet?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A third dirty register is the remaining way this address family could still beat the coordinate bill of eight.
open_questions.first_step: Stream a meet-in-the-middle: store hashes of the 231,812 radius-3 operators and test radius-4 predecessors of the target without retaining the radius-4 ball.
open_questions.blocked_by: A direct radius-4 enumeration was killed above 14 GB before a join existed.

open_questions.question: Does every register count still need four paid calls per central copy?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A uniform lower bound would close the scratch-register question without another census and would match the shape of the order-2 commutator theorems.
open_questions.first_step: Decide whether the length-3 coefficient of epsilon^4 in F2[epsilon]/(epsilon^5) vanishes for every rank-one idempotent.
open_questions.blocked_by: The nested projector polynomials are not identically zero, and no rank-one cancellation identity was proved here.
